title: Links
text:
Linking to a website
Use links to direct participants to external websites or online resources. Use descriptive link text that tells participants where the link will take them or what information they will find.
Markdown syntax
For more information,[visit the SciLifeLab website](https://www.scilifelab.se/)
Rendered result
For more information, visit the SciLifeLab website

title: Links
section: Linking to another page within your training repository
text:
Linking to another page within your training repository
You can link directly to another page in your training website. Use the relative path to the page, including its .qmd filename. Quarto will resolve the link to the corresponding rendered page when the website is built.
Markdown syntax
[Go to the introduction of Module 3](/content/module-3/introduction.qmd)
Rendered result
Go to the introduction of Module 3

title: Links
section: Linking to a file or resource within your training repository
text:
Linking to a file or resource within your training repository
You can link to files, such as PDF documents or other downloadable resources. Place the file in the docs folder at the root of your training repository. When linking to it from a page inside a content/module folder, use ../../docs/ followed by the filename. Adjust the path if your file is stored elsewhere.
Replace the example filename and path with those of your own file.
Markdown syntax
([Download the participant guide](../../docs/example-pdf.pdf))
Rendered result
Download the participant guide

title: Links
text:
Linking to resources hosted elsewhere
You can also link to resources hosted outside your training repository, such as presentations and documents in Google Slides or Google Docs. This allows participants to view or make a copy of a resource without you having to add the file to your repository.
For Google Slides and Google Docs, you can use the document ID from its URL to create different links. The document ID is the long string of letters and numbers between /d/ and the next / in the URL.
For example, a Google Slides URL may look like this:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/DOCUMENT_ID/edit
Replace DOCUMENT_ID with the ID from your own presentation.

Providing a view link
Use the /view ending to link directly to the presentation or document.
HTML syntax
<a href="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/DOCUMENT_ID/view" target="_blank">
  View in Google Slides
</a>
Rendered result
View in Google Slides


Providing a copy link
For Google Slides and Google Docs, you can use /copy to let participants create their own copy of a resource.
HTML syntax
<a href="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/DOCUMENT_ID/copy" target="_blank">
  Make a copy
</a>
Rendered result
Make a copy
You can use the same approach for Google Docs by replacing presentation in the URL with document.






Note



Participants may need to sign in to their Google account and have permission to access the original resource. Check the sharing settings before distributing the link.

title: Images, presentations and videos
text:
Adding images
Use images to illustrate concepts, show examples, or provide visual guidance. Add descriptive text that will be displayed as a caption. You can also resize and align images.
Place the image in the docs folder at the root of your training repository. From a page inside a module folder, use ../../docs/ followed by the image filename. Replace the example filename and text with your own.

Basic image
Markdown syntax
![A descriptive text explaining what the image shows](../../docs/example-image.svg)
Rendered result



A descriptive text explaining what the image shows


To remove the caption, simply remove the text between the brackets, for example:
![](../../docs/example-image.svg)


Resizing an image
You can set the width of an image using Quarto’s width attribute. For example, use width="10%" to display the image at 10% of the available text width.
Markdown syntax
![A descriptive text explaining what the image shows](../../docs/example-image.svg){width="10%"}
Rendered result



A descriptive text explaining what the image shows




Aligning an image
You can align an image to the left, center, or right using Quarto’s fig-align attribute.
Markdown syntax
![A descriptive text explaining what the image shows](../../docs/example-image.svg){fig-align="left"}
Rendered result



A descriptive text explaining what the image shows

title: Images, presentations and videos
text:
Embedding a presentation
You can embed a presentation so participants can view it directly on the training page, rather than following a link to another website. Presentation platforms such as PowerPoint or Google Slides provide embed code that you can add to your page.
For example, see how to find the embed code in Google Slides (from 1:41).
HTML syntax
<iframe
  src="PASTE-YOUR-PRESENTATION-EMBED-URL-HERE"
  width="100%"
  height="500"
  frameborder="0"
  allowfullscreen>
</iframe>
Rendered result

title: Images, presentations and videos
text:
Embedding videos
You can add a video file to your training repository and display it with a video player. The controls attribute allows participants to play, pause, and adjust the volume.
HTML syntax
<video controls width="100%">
  <source src="../../docs/example-video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  Your browser does not support the video element.
</video>
Rendered result

  
  Your browser does not support the video element.


Place the video file in the docs folder at the root of your training repository. Replace the example filename with the name of your video file.
You can also embed videos hosted on platforms such as YouTube or Vimeo. Use the embed code provided by the platform, in the same way as for presentations. For example, see see how to find the embed code for YouTube videos (from 0:18).

Use the training content pages to provide learning materials and activities for your training participants.
You can organise the pages to suit the structure of your training (for example: by day, module, topic, or section) or structure them around what participants need to learn and do.
In this template, the pages demonstrate how to use Markdown and Quarto to organise and format content. Use them as examples when creating your own training pages: find an example that suits your needs, copy the code snippet, and replace the demonstration text with your own. This way, you can build your pages without having to write Markdown from scratch.
The template pages cover:

Module 1 – How to structure a page: Headings, paragraphs, text formatting, lists, tables, code blocks and other content elements.
Module 2 – How to highlight information: Callouts for tips, notes, important information, and warnings.
Module 3 – How to add media and interactive elements: Links, images, documents, and videos.


If you want to learn more about Markdown, check out these free resources:

Markdown Guide – A practical guide to writing Markdown.
Markdown Cheatsheet – A quick reference to common Markdown syntax.
Markdown Tutorial – An interactive introduction to Markdown.
StackEdit – An in-browser Markdown editor.

Use a collapsible callout to place supplementary information that readers can expand when they want to see more. This is useful for optional details, explanations, or answers to questions.
Each example below shows the Quarto syntax and how the callout appears when rendered.

title: Collapsible callout boxes
text:
Collapsible note
Add collapse="true" to a callout to make it collapsible. The callout is initially collapsed, and readers can expand it to view the content.
Markdown syntax
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## More information

This content is hidden until the reader expands the section.
:::
Rendered result






More information





This content is hidden until the reader expands the section.

title: Collapsible callout boxes
text:
Nested callouts
You can place one callout inside another to group related information. For example, use a regular callout to introduce a topic, then place a collapsible callout inside it for supplementary details.
Markdown syntax
::: {.callout-note}
## Working with supplementary information

The expandable tip below provides an additional suggestion.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## More information

Save your work regularly so you do not lose your changes.
:::

:::
Rendered result






Working with supplementary information



The expandable tip below provides an additional suggestion.






More information





Save your work regularly so you do not lose your changes.

title: Callout boxes

title: Callout boxes
text:
Warning

title: Callout boxes
text:
Using callouts effectively
Callouts are optional. Use them when highlighting information improves the learning experience. Avoid adding too many to a page, as this can make it harder for readers to identify what is important. You can also include Markdown formatting, such as bold text, lists, or links, inside a callout.
Markdown syntax
::: {.callout-tip}
**Before submitting your work:**

- Check that all required sections are complete.
- Review your text for clarity.
- Save your changes.
:::
Rendered result

Use headings, paragraphs, and text formatting to organise your training content and make it easier for participants to read.

title: Headings and text
text:
Headings
Use headings to divide your page into sections and subsections. Quarto supports several heading levels:

## Main section — appears in the table of contents.
### Subsection — does not appear in the table of contents.
#### Sub-subsection — does not appear in the table of contents.

In this template, ## headings are displayed with a line underneath.
Markdown syntax
## Main section

Text introducing the section.

### Subsection

More detailed information.

#### Sub-subsection

Additional details.
Rendered result

Main section

Text introducing the section.

Subsection

More detailed information.

Sub-subsection

Additional details.
Use heading levels in order. For example, use ### for a subsection within a ## section, and #### for a subsection within a ### section.

title: Headings and text
text:
Paragraphs
Write ordinary text as paragraphs. Leave a blank line between paragraphs.
Markdown syntax
This is the first paragraph. It introduces a topic or explains an idea.

This is the second paragraph. It appears separately from the first.
Rendered result
This is the first paragraph. It introduces a topic or explains an idea.
This is the second paragraph. It appears separately from the first.

title: Headings and text
text:
Text formatting
Use bold and italic text to emphasise words or phrases.
Markdown syntax
This is **bold text**.

This is *italic text*.

This is ***bold and italic text***.
Rendered result
This is bold text.
This is italic text.
This is bold and italic text.

title: Lists and tables
text:
Bulleted lists
Use a hyphen (-) at the beginning of each line to create a bulleted list. Bulleted lists are useful for presenting related points that do not need to be followed in a particular order.
Markdown syntax
- First item
- Second item
- Third item
Rendered result

First item
Second item
Third item


Nested lists
Indent items to create a list within a list. Use nested lists to show how information is grouped.
Markdown syntax
- Main item
  - Supporting point
  - Another supporting point
- Another main item
Rendered result

Main item

Supporting point
Another supporting point

Another main item

title: Lists and tables
text:
Numbered lists
Use numbers followed by a period when the order of the items matters, such as for instructions or a process.
Markdown syntax
1. Open the training page.
2. Find the section you want to update.
3. Replace the example text with your own content.
4. Render the website and review the result.
Rendered result

Find the section you want to update.
Replace the example text with your own content.
Render the website and review the result.

title: Lists and tables
text:
Tables
Use tables to present information in rows and columns, especially when you want participants to compare related details. Use clear column headings and keep the content concise.
Markdown syntax
| Element | Purpose | Example |

| Heading | Introduces a section | Learning objectives |
| Paragraph | Explains an idea | A short description |
| List | Groups related items | Steps or key points |
